Israel Eliyahou Suissa, son of Hava Parha and Moshe, was born on the 29th of Av 5763 (27 August 2003) in Montreal, Canada. He was the brother of ten: Salma, Yosef, Menachem, Miriam, Hiya, Haim, Levi, Mazal, Menuha and Netanel.

Israel Eliyahou grew up and was educated in Montreal. In July 2016 the family made aliyah and settled in the Krayot, north of Haifa. He studied at the Chabad institutions in Kiryat Shmuel until eighth grade, and in ninth grade he transferred to the Levinson High School in Kiryat Yam.

He was a clever boy, full of charm and joie de vivre. His father described him as "a positive and smiling person, one who never gives up and nothing scares him." His outlook on life was optimistic; he never complained about what had happened, but always looked for the positive side of everything. His sister Hiya said: "My brother knew how to make a joke out of anything. He always knew how to lighten the mood for everyone and lift the atmosphere. He knew how to make everyone around him smile."

Determined and energetic, he liked to set himself challenges and goals and to pursue them with persistence and consistency. His high school teacher, Meir, noted this special character: "He was a boy who had every reason to throw up his hands, but he never did. I learned something new from him every day. He always expressed his wishes in the most genuine and pure way possible. I never heard him say that things were hard for him. He learned to look at things in a healthy way, with a constant smile on his face."

Israel was a sports fan, especially of ice hockey, football and calisthenics. He used to play hockey on rollerblades in the park and train in the gym. In his free time he enjoyed playing the piano for his friends in the living room of his home and playing snooker with them. He was active in the youth movement "Achrei!" in the Kiryat Haim group.

His faith was very strong. All his life he adhered to the Torah and its commandments, and he would put on tefillin every morning, feeling a sense of purification during prayer.

On 16 December 2021 he enlisted in the IDF and volunteered for combat service as a fighter in the Paratroopers Brigade in the Infantry Corps. He completed various training courses and served in his unit as a gunner (responsible for the Negev machine gun). A professional and dedicated soldier, he was "an asset to the class and the team," in the words of his commander.

He was recognized as a lone soldier, since his family had moved to Canada before his enlistment. Despite the difficulty involved, he decided to stay in the country and fulfill his dream of enlisting for combat service. He was highly motivated to carry out his tasks successfully, and felt a sense of meaning and mission in his role.

He lived in "Benny's House" in Ra'anana, a home for lone soldiers. He loved the country and the army, had high morale, and helped the other lone soldiers in every matter.

On Shabbat, 22 Tishri, Simchat Torah 5784, 7 October 2023, at half past six in the morning, the terrorist organization Hamas launched a surprise attack on Israel. Under cover of massive rocket and missile fire from the Gaza Strip into wide areas of the country, thousands of terrorists infiltrated by land, sea and air, and launched a murderous assault on the communities of the Gaza envelope and on Sderot, Ofakim and Netivot, on the Nova music festival near the kibbutzim Re'im and Nir Am, on IDF bases and on travelers on the roads in the area. The terrorists murdered some eight hundred civilians in their homes and in their cars, after committing grave crimes against them. Hundreds of Israelis were abducted into the Gaza Strip, and homes and property were destroyed, looted and set on fire. Hundreds of soldiers, police officers, security personnel and members of local emergency squads fell in battle. That morning, a war began.

With the entry of the IDF into the Gaza Strip and the start of the ground maneuver in late October 2023, Israel fought intensively alongside his comrades for many long months. He took part in fierce battles in almost every sector, from the north of the Strip: Beit Lahia, Beit Hanoun, Jabalia, Gaza City, the central camps and the south, along the Philadelphi Corridor and in Rafah. His commander testified that he would say "we can keep going" even when it was hard for him, as evidence of his dedication and seriousness.

On 5 March 2024, during a week-long break from the fighting, while riding a motorcycle on his way to "Benny's House" in Ra'anana, Israel was killed in a road accident.

Sergeant First Class Israel Eliyahou Suissa fell during his service in the war on 26 Adar I 5784 (5 March 2024). He was twenty years old at his death. He was laid to rest in the military cemetery in Haifa. He left behind parents and ten brothers and sisters.

Israel is commemorated at the Paratroopers Memorial near the Beit Lid Junction.
